title: A new choroidal mass decades after breast surgery
task_type: A new choroidal mass decades after breast surgery
summary: An 83-year-old woman presents with reduced vision in her left eye. She underwent radical mastectomy for breast ductal carcinoma in situ 31 years earlier; the report describes a primary lesion under 2 mm and negative margins. Examination now describes a non-pigmented choroidal mass surrounding the optic disc, measuring 9 × 7 × 2.4 mm, with subretinal fluid. A comparable lesion was not seen at the examination one year earlier. No aspiration result, systemic staging result or subsequent treatment outcome is provided.
purpose: Write 160–220 words for a clinician. Summarise the current ocular problem, compare reasonable diagnostic categories and explain how the remote breast history should affect the assessment. State the evidence needed before attributing the lesion to a particular origin. Do not treat the long interval or previous in-situ label as proof against malignancy, but do not assert a metastatic origin without the withheld evidence. Do not invent current systemic disease or propose a fixed treatment regimen.

case.hidden:
Adaptation, hidden results and review

This draft stops before tissue confirmation. Published descriptive findings are used in text; the diagnostic title, cytology panel/caption, immunostains and referral are hidden. The report later describes aspiration confirming breast carcinoma with AE1/3, EMA and GATA3 positivity, followed by referral for radiotherapy and systemic oncological assessment. It does not establish a genetic lineage comparison with the original lesion or supply detailed systemic staging outcomes; neither is added to the reference.
